questions.question: Which river is the national river of India?
questions.funFact: The Ganga travels more than 2,500 kilometres before reaching the sea.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal is found in which city?
questions.funFact: Thousands of workers and elephants took over 20 years to build the Taj Mahal.

questions.question: Which festival is called the 'festival of colours'?
questions.funFact: Holi is celebrated in spring, when fields are full of colourful flowers.

questions.question: The Himalayas are in the northern part of India.
questions.funFact: The Himalayas act like a giant wall that protects India from cold winds coming from the north.

questions.question: The Thar Desert is mainly found in the state of ___.
questions.funFact: The Thar Desert is one of the most crowded deserts in the world, with many villages in it.

questions.question: What is the capital of Assam?
questions.funFact: Assam is famous for its tea gardens and for the one-horned rhinoceros.

questions.question: Match each monument to its city.
questions.funFact: India's monuments were built by many different rulers over hundreds of years.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a river?
questions.funFact: The Aravalli is a mountain range, while the other three are rivers.

questions.question: During Diwali, people light small oil lamps called ___.
questions.funFact: Diwali is also a time when families clean their homes and share sweets with neighbours.

questions.question: Onam is a festival celebrated mainly in Kerala.
questions.funFact: Onam remembers a kind and much-loved king named Mahabali.

questions.question: The Statue of Unity honours which great leader?
questions.funFact: Sardar Patel helped join hundreds of small kingdoms together to make one united India.

questions.question: Arrange these places along the Ganga's journey, from where it starts to where it ends.
questions.funFact: A river always flows downhill, from high mountains all the way down to the sea.

questions.question: Which is the highest mountain peak in India?
questions.funFact: Kanchenjunga stands on the border of Sikkim and is the third-highest mountain in the world.

questions.question: The 'Seven Sisters' states are found in the ___ part of India.
questions.funFact: Sikkim is sometimes called the 'brother' of the seven North-Eastern sisters.

questions.question: The Rann of Kutch is a white salt desert in Gujarat.
questions.funFact: On full-moon nights, the white salt of the Rann of Kutch shines brightly under the moonlight.
